guide.summary: Forgejo documents an OAuth2 provider with the Authorization Code grant, PKCE and confidential or public clients, so the OAuth path for a per-customer instance is supported. OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token acts with the connected user's full account access rather than a read-only grant. Third-party OAuth applications receive administrative rights, which must be disclosed. The documented repository list endpoint returns repositories the user owns and is paginated. Whether it covers all repositories visible to the person is not established by the supplied passages.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List repository names visible to the connected person, with pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Authorization Code grant with PKCE and confidential or public clients is documented
findings.detail: Forgejo supports the Authorization Code Grant with PKCE and supports both confidential and public OAuth2 client types. Public clients use PKCE and must be registered as public clients.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when the customer's Forgejo instance is the OAuth2 provider for this integration.

evidence.quote: Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:
Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

findings.title: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented; tokens act with the user's full access
findings.detail: Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to execute any action on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions. The token boundary is therefore the connected person's account access, and the read-only intent of this request is not enforced by the token.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to every OAuth2 token issued by the customer's Forgejo instance for this integration.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Note Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to
execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.

findings.title: Third-party applications obtaining a token via OAuth2 receive administrative rights
findings.detail: The provider documentation states that third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via an OAuth2 application will have administrative rights. This is broader than the read-only repository listing requested and must be disclosed to the customer before setup.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when the token is issued through a Forgejo OAuth2 application on the customer instance.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.
Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

findings.title: Customer must register an OAuth2 application and configure its redirect URI
findings.detail: To use the Authorization Code grant, a new application must be registered in the user settings applications section, which yields a client ID and secret. The redirect URI must match between the authorize and access token requests.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies before the first connection test on each customer instance.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.

findings.title: Bearer tokens from the OAuth2 provider are accepted by the API
findings.detail: OAuth2 provider access tokens are accepted in the Authorization Bearer header or in token or access_token query parameters. The integration must send the access token in one of these forms.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to every API request made with an OAuth2-issued access token.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 Provider Access tokens obtained from Forgejo’s OAuth2 provider are accepted by these methods:
Authorization: Bearer ... header in HTTP headers
token=... parameter in URL query string

steps.title: Register OAuth2 application on the customer instance
steps.detail: The customer registers an OAuth2 application at their own Forgejo instance settings page (/user/settings/applications), choosing confidential or public client type and a redirect URI. Disclose that third-party OAuth tokens carry administrative rights and that OAuth2 scopes are not enforced.
steps.doneWhen: The customer holds a client ID and client secret (confidential) or client ID (public) for a registered application with the redirect URI set.

steps.title: Run authorization consent redirect and verify callback
steps.detail: Send the connected person to the authorization endpoint with the client ID, redirect URI, response_type=code and a state value. The user must approve. Verify the callback returns code and the same state before any token exchange.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect returns to REDIRECT_URI with code and matching state; no token has been requested yet.

sent back to your application after the user authorizes. The state parameter is optional but should be used to prevent CSRF attacks.
The user will now be asked to authorize your application. If they authorize it, the user will be redirected to the REDIRECT_URL , for example:

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

STATE: random string generated by the integration

steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token, token_type bearer, expires_in and refresh_token.

details.title: Authorization Code grant with PKCE and confidential or public clients is documented
details.detail: Forgejo supports the Authorization Code Grant with PKCE and supports both confidential and public OAuth2 client types. Public clients use PKCE and must be registered as public clients.
details.appliesWhen: Applies when the customer's Forgejo instance is the OAuth2 provider for this integration.

evidence.quote: Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:
Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

details.title: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented; tokens act with the user's full access
details.detail: Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to execute any action on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions. The token boundary is therefore the connected person's account access, and the read-only intent of this request is not enforced by the token.
details.appliesWhen: Applies to every OAuth2 token issued by the customer's Forgejo instance for this integration.

details.title: Third-party applications obtaining a token via OAuth2 receive administrative rights
details.detail: The provider documentation states that third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via an OAuth2 application will have administrative rights. This is broader than the read-only repository listing requested and must be disclosed to the customer before setup.
details.appliesWhen: Applies when the token is issued through a Forgejo OAuth2 application on the customer instance.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.
Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register OAuth2 application on the customer instance
The customer registers an OAuth2 application at their own Forgejo instance settings page (/user/settings/applications), choosing confidential or public client type and a redirect URI. Disclose that third-party OAuth tokens carry administrative rights and that OAuth2 scopes are not enforced.
Fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: customer's full HTTPS Forgejo base URL, user-provided, CLIENT_ID: from the registered application, user-provided, CLIENT_SECRET: from the registered application, user-provided (confidential only), REDIRECT_URI: must match the value registered

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Run authorization consent redirect and verify callback
Done when: The redirect returns to REDIRECT_URI with code and matching state; no token has been requested yet.

Exchange authorization code for access token
Done when: The response contains access_token, token_type bearer, expires_in and refresh_token.

Hold repository visibility listing as unresolved
Done when: Coverage remains unresolved until a supplied, documented endpoint lists all repositories visible to the connected person. Boundary check: confirm no request was sent and no create, edit or delete operation occurred.

Request next page of repository names until documented end
Done when: Pagination ends when the response Link header has no rel=next entry, and the total of names matches X-Total-Count. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

Confirm read-only boundary without executing writes
Done when: Customer confirms only GET requests were sent and understands the token has full account access.

Continue pagination until documented end condition
Done when: No rel=next Link header remains. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
